stem: An intestinal transplant recipient develops a new rash weeks after transplant. Which complication should the coordinator include in the differential?

options.text: Graft-versus-host disease presenting most commonly as a skin rash
Expected benign finding that never involves skin after intestine transplant
Hyperacute rejection that occurs only years after transplant
Oral aversion, which never presents with cutaneous findings

explanation.rationale_correct: Graft-versus-host disease after intestinal transplantation presents most commonly as a skin rash but may also involve the liver and gastrointestinal tract and can occur from days to years post-transplant.

rationale_incorrect.B: Skin rash is the most common presentation of GVHD in intestine recipients.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hyperacute rejection occurs immediately after implantation rather than weeks to years later.
rationale_incorrect.D: Oral aversion is a feeding complication distinct from the cutaneous GVHD presentation described.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Intestine Transplantation → 8. Graft-versus-host disease → d.–e.

stem: A heart transplant recipient develops declining ejection fraction and heart-failure symptoms months after transplant. Which etiology should the coordinator recognize as a potential cause of left ventricular systolic dysfunction?

options.text: Donor blood-type incompatibility discovered only at one-year anniversary
Expected normal healing that never affects ejection fraction
Pretransplant evaluation error unrelated to allograft pathology

explanation.rationale_correct: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction in heart transplant recipients may result from ischemic or reperfusion injury, primary graft dysfunction, coronary artery vasculopathy, or cellular or humoral rejection.

rationale_incorrect.B: ABO compatibility is established before transplant; late LV dysfunction is evaluated for allograft causes such as CAV or rejection.
rationale_incorrect.C: Declining ejection fraction and heart-failure symptoms warrant evaluation for graft dysfunction rather than assumed benign healing.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant LV dysfunction is assessed for allograft-related etiologies including vasculopathy and rejection.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 9, Heart Transplantation → LV systolic dysfunction → 1. Etiology → f.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Coronary artery vasculopathy … Cellular or humoral rejection

stem: A pediatric kidney transplant recipient has prolonged acute tubular necrosis (ATN) with oliguria. Evaluate the following monitoring and management statements:

elements.text: During prolonged ATN, serial renal biopsies may be performed to assess kidney function and monitor for rejection.
ATN may last for variable periods from hours up to several weeks.
Management includes avoiding nephrotoxic drugs and conservative fluid replacement to prevent hypervolemia.
Hyperkalemia never occurs during pediatric ATN because potassium is automatically excreted.

explanation.rationale_correct: Pediatric ATN may persist for hours to weeks; prolonged ATN warrants serial biopsies to assess function and exclude rejection; management includes avoiding nephrotoxic drugs and conservative fluids. Hyperkalemia develops rapidly in anuric patients, so statement IV is false.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also correct—management includes avoiding nephrotoxic drugs and preventing hypervolemia.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement IV is false; close potassium monitoring is emphasized during pediatric ATN.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false; anuric patients quickly become hyperkalemic.

stem: When counseling a kidney transplant recipient about routine trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis, which additional infection-prevention benefit aligns with standard references?

options.text: Effectiveness against Toxoplasma gondii in addition to Pneumocystis jiroveci
Prevention of all viral infections including cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr virus
Guaranteed prevention of acute cellular rejection episodes

explanation.rationale_correct: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is routinely used to prevent Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonitis and is also effective for preventing Toxoplasma gondii, selected Nocardia species, and Listeria monocytogenes.

rationale_incorrect.B: Antiviral agents, not TMP-SMX, address CMV and EBV prevention strategies.
rationale_incorrect.C: Antimicrobial prophylaxis supplements rather than replaces immunosuppressive therapy.
rationale_incorrect.D: Antimicrobial prophylaxis prevents selected infections but does not prevent rejection.
